nominees.name: Hideo Hosono
nominees.affiliation: Tokyo Institute of Technology (Institute of Science Tokyo), Japan

motivation: In 2008 Hideo Hosono and co-workers reported superconductivity at 26 K in fluorine-doped LaFeAsO. Within months, transition temperatures above 50 K followed, giving the second family of high-temperature superconductors after the cuprates. Few had expected iron, usually hostile to superconductivity, to host it. The discovery was the result of a deliberate programme of designing layered mixed-anion compounds. It opened a very large materials space, with pnictides and chalcogenides, clean single crystals and tunable doping and pressure. That space made it possible to test universal ideas cleanly: spin-fluctuation pairing, sign-changing gap symmetry, quantum criticality under the superconducting dome, and electronic nematicity. It also produced monolayer FeSe and practical wires. Like the cuprates and high-mobility GaAs, this is a case where a new material changed what the community believes is possible in real solids. It merits the Nobel Prize.
